# model

manage models: built-ins, aliases, custom endpoints

Manage the models coder can dispatch to. `add` connects any OpenAI-compatible
endpoint (Ollama, vLLM, OpenRouter, ...) as the custom engine, alongside the
built-in codex/claude models. Name your own shortcuts with `alias`
(e.g. fast -> codex/luna); disable/enable turns any model off and on.

## `model list [--server <server>] [--workspace <workspace>] [--yes] [--json] [--cwd <cwd>]`

list built-ins, custom models, and aliases

List built-in aliases, configured custom models, and user aliases. Only custom
models on this machine are probed; --server lists the workspace's.

- `--server <server>` act on the Coder server
- `--workspace <workspace>` with --server: the workspace to act in (default: the saved one)
- `--yes` with --server: connect to a server used for the first time without asking
- `--json` JSON output
- `--cwd <cwd>` workspace directory; default current

## `model add [name] [--base-url <base-url>] [--model <model>] [--env-key <env-key>] [--context-window <context-window>] [--workspace] [--json] [--cwd <cwd>]`

connect a model

Connect a custom model behind an OpenAI-compatible endpoint (Ollama, LM Studio,
vLLM, OpenRouter, ...). It currently runs on the codex engine pointed at your
URL and is usable anywhere a model is: --model <name> or --model custom/<name>, or as an
agent default in config. Alias: `coder model setup`.

- `<name>` the name to dispatch it by
- `--base-url <base-url>` OpenAI-compatible API base (e.g. http://localhost:11434/v1)
- `--model <model>` the provider's model id (e.g. qwen2.5-coder:32b)
- `--env-key <env-key>` env var holding the API key (omit for keyless local endpoints)
- `--context-window <context-window>` the model's context window in tokens; filled from the provider when it reports one
- `--workspace` write to <repo>/.coder/config.json instead of the user file
- `--json` JSON output
- `--cwd <cwd>` workspace directory; default current

```sh
coder model add qwen --base-url http://localhost:11434/v1 --model qwen2.5-coder:32b  # local Ollama model, no key
coder model add kimi --base-url https://openrouter.ai/api/v1 --model moonshotai/kimi-k2 --env-key OPENROUTER_API_KEY  # third-party provider via OpenRouter
coder run --model qwen "explain this repo"  # dispatch a task on it
```

## `model update [name] [--base-url <base-url>] [--model <model>] [--env-key <env-key>] [--context-window <context-window>] [--workspace] [--json] [--cwd <cwd>]`

change a model in place

Update a configured custom model. Only the flags you pass change; the endpoint
is re-probed and the wire protocol re-detected.

- `<name>` the custom model
- `--base-url <base-url>` new API base
- `--model <model>` new provider model id
- `--env-key <env-key>` new API-key env var
- `--context-window <context-window>` the model's context window in tokens; filled from the provider when it reports one
- `--workspace` write to <repo>/.coder/config.json instead of the user file
- `--json` JSON output
- `--cwd <cwd>` workspace directory; default current

## `model remove [name] [--workspace] [--json] [--cwd <cwd>]`

delete a custom model

Remove a configured custom model.

- `<name>` the custom model
- `--workspace` target <repo>/.coder/config.json instead of the user file
- `--json` JSON output
- `--cwd <cwd>` workspace directory; default current

## `model disable [name] [--workspace] [--json] [--cwd <cwd>]`

turn off a model (built-in, custom, or alias)

Disable a model - built-in, custom, or alias. Requests for it fail until re-enabled.

- `<name>` a built-in, custom model, or alias
- `--workspace` target <repo>/.coder/config.json instead of the user file
- `--json` JSON output
- `--cwd <cwd>` workspace directory; default current

## `model enable [name] [--workspace] [--json] [--cwd <cwd>]`

re-enable a disabled model

- `<name>` a built-in, custom model, or alias
- `--workspace` target <repo>/.coder/config.json instead of the user file
- `--json` JSON output
- `--cwd <cwd>` workspace directory; default current

## `model alias [name] [spec] [--workspace] [--json] [--cwd <cwd>]`

name a spec, e.g. fast codex/luna

Save an alias for an engine spec, e.g. fast -> codex/luna. An alias may reuse a
built-in name to override it; an engine name sets what that bare engine runs.

- `<name>` the alias
- `<spec>` the engine spec, such as codex/luna
- `--workspace` target <repo>/.coder/config.json instead of the user file
- `--json` JSON output
- `--cwd <cwd>` workspace directory; default current

## `model unalias [name] [--workspace] [--json] [--cwd <cwd>]`

remove an alias

Remove a user-defined alias.

- `<name>` the alias
- `--workspace` target <repo>/.coder/config.json instead of the user file
- `--json` JSON output
- `--cwd <cwd>` workspace directory; default current
